After the massive real estate expansion in the South Bay area in 2025, Apple is once again expanding its business presence in Sunnyvale. Details below.

Apple continues to expand its business footprint

According to a report by The Mercury News (republished by AppleInsider), Apple has agreed to lease an office building of 125,800 square feet at 580 North Mathilda Avenue in Sunnyvale.

This deal is Apple's first major real estate move in the area in 2026. In 2025, Apple spent more than US$1 billion expanding its presence in the South Bay area, making it a particularly busy year.

These include the purchase of three buildings at the Cupertino Gateway for US$166.9 million, the acquisition of two buildings at Mathilda Commons in Sunnyvale for US$350 million, as well as the purchase of four adjacent buildings at Mathilda Campus for US$365 million.

Apple subsequently invested another US$216 million in two buildings on Stevens Creek Boulevard in Cupertino, bringing its Bay Area expansion in 2025 to more than 1.5 million square feet of office and laboratory space in total.

Returning to Apple's new lease, The Mercury News noted that this deal comes as office leasing activity in the South Bay area begins to pick up, with vacancy rates improving compared to the previous quarter and the same period last year:

According to a report by Colliers, the office vacancy rate in the South Bay area was 14.1% in the second quarter of 2026. Colliers defines the market as covering Santa Clara County and Fremont. This represents an improvement from the 14.8% vacancy rate in the fourth quarter of October to December 2025, as well as the 16.2% vacancy rate in the second quarter of 2025.

Apart from Apple, the report also mentioned that Amazon has agreed to lease 316,600 square feet of office space located at 1000 Enterprise Way in Sunnyvale.
